transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Refrigerant systems in domestic fridges are sealed and require specialist recovery equipment and certification to handle legally and safely. Attempting this yourself is dangerous, illegal under F-Gas regulations, and will probably not fix the problem if it isn't a simple leak (which is rare). If there is a refrigerant leak, it requires an engineer. The most common cause for this specific pattern on a frost-free fridge-freezer is actually a blocked airflow due to ice build-up inside the freezer, often caused by a failed defrost heater or thermostat. 1. Is the freezer compartment still cold (or freezing) while only the fridge is warm, or are both compartments completely warm?
both are warm. freezer is about 0C and everything has thawed, fridge about 13C. compressor never switches off just hums non stop

Since both compartments are warm while the compressor runs constantly, we have ruled out simple settings issues. The fact that the compressor never switches off suggests it is trying hard to reach a temperature it can't achieve. The two most likely causes now are:
1. Sealed system failure: The compressor is running but not pumping refrigerant effectively (either due to internal wear or a leak). This requires an engineer and cannot be fixed with a DIY gas kit.
2. Evaporator fan fault: In frost-free models, a fan pushes cold air from the freezer into the fridge. If this fan has stopped, the freezer might stay slightly cooler (0°C) while the fridge warms up, but eventually, everything will go warm as the ice melts and the compressor runs endlessly. To tell these apart safely: With both doors closed, listen carefully inside the freezer compartment for a faint whirring or humming sound coming from behind the back panel. Is there a fan running (even quietly), or is it completely silent?
yeah i can hear a fan going when the door's shut. so is it the gas then or not?

To answer your question directly: no, it is not just a case of needing 'gas'. As I mentioned, you cannot simply top up the gas; if there is a leak, it needs to be found and repaired by an engineer, or the whole sealed system replaced. If the compressor is running but not cooling effectively, it usually means the compressor itself has lost its pumping power (internal wear) rather than just being 'low on gas'. However, before we conclude that the compressor is dead (which would mean replacing the entire unit is often more cost-effective than repairing), we need to rule out a very common issue: ice blocking the airflow. 1. Unplug the appliance and leave both doors open for 24 hours to ensure all internal ice melts completely.
2. Plug it back in and let it run empty (no food inside) for at least 6-8 hours.
3. Check if the freezer gets cold again. If it cools down perfectly after this, the issue was a blocked defrost system (likely a faulty heater or thermostat), which an engineer can fix without checking the compressor. If it remains warm despite being fully defrosted and running for 24 hours, then the sealed system has failed.

do i really have to wait 24 hrs?? everything's already thawed so theres no ice in there to melt. i did chip ice out of the freezer with a knife a few months back tho, and the rating plate says R600a if that matters

You don't need to wait 24 hours if there is no ice left. 1. This cannot be fixed with a DIY kit; it requires an engineer or replacement of the unit.
2. Ice has built up inside the freezer's back panel, blocking the fan from pushing air into the fridge compartment. To tell these apart: Please look at the rear wall inside the freezer (you may need to remove shelves). Is there a solid block of white ice covering the coils/panel, or is it clear? If it is iced up, that suggests a defrost fault. If it looks clear but the fridge still doesn't cool after a proper reset, it is probably the sealed system failing.
no ice at all, no frost anywhere. the back wall of the freezer isn't even cold, just bare. so whats that mean, is it the sealed system then?

Yes, given that the fan is running but there is no ice and the back wall of the freezer isn't cold, it is probably a sealed system failure. This is why both compartments are warming up despite the motor working hard. The system uses R600a (isobutane), which is highly flammable and requires specialist recovery equipment to handle safely and legally under F-Gas regulations. Furthermore, simply adding gas will not work; if the compressor has lost its internal pumping power, it needs replacement or the entire unit needs replacing. At this stage, repair costs for a sealed system fault (new compressor, cleaning pipes, recharging gas) are typically very high—often close to the price of a new appliance. Unless your fridge-freezer is under 3–4 years old and still covered by a manufacturer's warranty or an extended guarantee that covers parts like the compressor, it is usually more cost-effective to replace the unit rather than call out an engineer for a repair.
